summary: Embedding ingest normalization mismatch causing rerank order flips and latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Customer (StreamlineAI) reports intermittent rerank order flips and pronounced latency spikes on rerank endpoint after bulk embedding ingest job completed earlier today.
Impact: User-facing search results for a subset of collections show top-K reorder (relevant items demoted) and rerank calls experience CPU fallback path causing 2-8x token scoring latency; some requests time out and return 503s. Affects production collections in their dedicated pool.
Environment: prod:us-east-1, dedicated pool #dcp-37, ingest job ran against s3://streamlineai-embeds/2026-03-10/*.ndjson.
Observed behaviour: 1) sudden decrease in rerank quality (reproducible on a steady prompt set). 2) tail latency increase concurrent with ingest completion. 3) logs show dimension negotiation warnings and conversion routines triggered at scoring time.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) Trigger rerank endpoint /v1/rerank with the canonical prompt set provided (attached in support artifact).
4) Observe latency metrics in APM and request traces via Console > Rerank > Traces.
5) Re-run a synthetic rerank batch including newly ingested vectors to reproduce conversion log messages.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:23:12Z WARN embed-transformer: input_dim=1536 storage_dim=2048 -> padding detected; storing with pad_flag=1
2026-03-10T15:01:03Z ERROR reranker: dim_mismatch detected for doc_id=stream-qa-1123; spawning conversion_fallback_worker
2026-03-10T15:01:03Z INFO conversion_worker: performing upcast_pad_fix for doc_id=stream-qa-1123 (cpu path)
2026-03-10T15:01:04Z WARN api-gateway: request_id=rid-8f3 timeout_warning 1200ms (tail latency surge)
2026-03-10T15:01:05Z ERROR reranker: scoring_timeout for request_id=rid-8f3 return 503
observed_metrics: Rerank P99 latency increased from ~240ms to ~1.9s between 15:00-15:10 UTC
CPU worker utilization for conversion_worker spiked to 85% on pool dcp-37
initial_hypothesis: The ingest transform job wrote embeddings with a larger storage dimension (2048) and marked records with padding flags instead of normalizing to model-dimension (1536).

Reranker defers normalization until scoring; when it encounters padded vectors it triggers a CPU-based upcast/reshape conversion path that is slow and resource-heavy, causing tail latency and occasional timeouts.
Some vector-store reads return mixed-dimension batches which force per-document conversion rather than fast batched GPU scoring.
investigation_notes: Confirmed ingest job (ingest-transform v1.14) was updated on 2026-03-10 to write storage_dim=2048 for backward compatibility with an internal schema change.
S3 artifact sample: file 'batch-2026-03-10.ndjson' contains embeddings where metadata.dimension=1536 but payload length corresponds to 2048 floats -> mismatch flag present.
Reranker code path 'score_batch_gpu' checks header.dim == model.dim, if mismatch it routes to 'score_single_cpu_convert' which is not optimized for high QPS.
Temporary reproduction run on staging with mixed-dim dataset reproduced P99 spike and conversion_worker counts matching prod.
workaround: 1) Roll back ingest-transform to v1.13 which normalizes embeddings to model_dim before storing. Deployed to streamlining job and reprocessed two batches (confirmed improvement).
2) For affected collections, a scoped reindex job was run to rewrite stored vectors to target_dim=1536 (reindex id: reidx-2026-03-11-streamline).
3) Added emergency rate-limit increase on dedicated pool dcp-37 for conversion_worker to reduce request throttling during reindex.
resolution: Root cause: ingest-transform v1.14 introduced storage-dimension parity mode that wrote larger payloads and relied on pad_flag without normalizing at ingest. Reranker expected stored vectors to match model_dim or to be normalized at ingest; dimension mismatch triggered CPU conversion fallback path causing latency and order instability.

Fix deployed: ingest-transform v1.15 publishes normalized embeddings (ensures payload length == metadata.dimension) and sets a validation check in pipeline to reject mismatched records. Deployed 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC.

Reranker hotfix: added a fast-path vector-pad-trim routine in score_batch_gpu to handle trailing-zero padding without full conversion (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/789). Deployed 2026-03-11 06:30 UTC.
Customer impact: StreamlineAI reindex completed and quality metrics returned to baseline. No further 503s observed after 2026-03-11 07:00 UTC.
